A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GuidedSampling work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite added material and changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference and fine-tuning experiments, diversity measurements, exploration-budget analyses, and additional model results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Gemma results, CommonsenseQA evaluation, majority-vote accuracy, concept-order analysis, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The two-phase sampling algorithm, Algorithm 1, and FA/CAA training objectives remain unchanged. Section 5 and Appendix E.3 add majority-vote final-answer selection on top of sampled candidates, a limited inference-pipeline extension applied to all compared samplers.

E1.justification: v2 adds CommonsenseQA evaluation with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, extending coverage to commonsense questions without well-defined task-specific concepts. The original four evaluation benchmarks and OpenMathInstruct-2 training coverage remain. Additional Gemma experiments use retained tasks.

E2.justification: Tree-of-Thought is added to the primary inference pass@k comparisons in Figure 4 and participates in the new voting and call-cost comparisons. v1 already evaluated ToT for fine-tuning and diversity, but its main inference-performance comparison used only RS. The fine-tuning comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation of Gemma-3-27b-it, majority-vote accuracy, analysis conditional on reaching each concept index, a ten-candidate HumanEval stopping diagnostic, and average LLM-call measurements. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original sampling budgets and fine-tuning settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses examine earlier versus later concepts and their declining coverage, failure on CommonsenseQA, possible CAA model collapse through stopping behavior, and performance versus LLM calls. Figure 5 also extends the existing exploration-budget sensitivity analysis to Gemma. The original examples and irrelevant-concept case study remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical error bars. The training-split seed remains 21. v2 adds qualitative variability cautions and concept-index sample counts, but no new statistical uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Original results in Tables 1 and 6 and the existing Figure 4–5 series are retained, while extensive new results are added. Examples include Gemma GPQA pass@50 of 92.42% for GuidedSampling versus 70.20% for RS, CommonsenseQA scores of 95.66% versus 98.94%, and majority-vote averages of 35.87%, 32.80%, and 26.26% for GuidedSampling, RS, and ToT. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under changed settings.

T1.justification: Assumption 1 now explicitly applies to relevant concepts in Cr rather than informative concepts in Cinf, and its amplification equation changes from equality to a lower bound. Appendix A.1 adapts the derivation previously shown in the main text. The theorem and principal proof remain essentially unchanged; this is not a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: separating concept exploration from solution generation, improving sampling diversity and performance, and using these trajectories for post-training. Their headline numerical claims are also unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 develops an applicability boundary around whether useful concepts can be formulated, supported by the CommonsenseQA failure. It adds interpretations of concept-order effects and sparse late-concept coverage, discusses sequential exploration overhead, and introduces explicit limitations concerning model/domain coverage and selecting correct minority answers. Appendix F also adds a tentative no-collapse interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies CommonsenseQA prompts, discloses best-K selection in Figure 4, and identifies the finish-reason diagnostic used in Appendix F. Figure 4 additionally labels the math benchmark MATH-500; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, and code/data access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 updates agentic and reinforcement-learning citations, adds references for Gemma, CommonsenseQA, and model collapse, and removes Estornell and Liu. The central positioning against repeated sampling, tree search, and RandIdeaInjection remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds discussion and limitations statements, subdivides Appendices A and E, appends I and J, corrects IAA to CAA in prompt headings, and updates publication and author information. These are localized expansions and organizational edits rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 5 expand to three model rows, with Figure 4 adding ToT curves and revised axes, legends, and captions. New Tables 7–10 and Figures 6–7 display additional evaluations, concept-order behavior, and call costs. Existing tables and examples are retained but reflowed or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation beyond v1's main RS comparison: it adds direct ToT comparisons, a larger model, final-answer voting tests, cost evidence, and an informative commonsense failure. These additions clarify practical benefits and applicability limits. Important weaknesses remain: Theorem 1 still claims equivalence from a sufficient lower-bound argument, and Appendix J's stated all-model averages match only the original two-model results. Nevertheless, the broader comparative evidence and explicit failure analysis provide a substantial net improvement.
